observations: Photo 0: A Nikon-branded box printed with 'D750', sitting on an orange sofa, next to a smaller 'Nikkor Lens 50' box and a large box showing a gimbal/stabilizer with a camera illustration.
Photo 1: The D750 box opened, showing only printed paper manuals ('D750 User's Manual', 'Manuel d'utilisation') and a small zhiyun-branded box visible in the background.
Photo 2: A box interior with items wrapped in bubble wrap; shapes are not identifiable as a camera body, only plastic-wrapped bulges.
No camera body, lens glass, LCD screen, lens mount, serial number plate, or power-on state is visible in any photo.
No hands, no live demonstration, no SD card, no shutter count, no battery shown.

claims.evidence: Only the retail box and manual carry the 'D750' print; the actual camera body is never shown unwrapped in any photo.
No import sticker, customs mark, or region-specific accessory shown.
No unobstructed photo of the body, lens mount, screen, or exterior finish.
No power-on shot, shutter count screen, or test image shown.

risks.risk: Box and manual could be genuine while the actual item inside is a different/older body, a damaged unit, or even missing entirely.
risks.proof: A photo of the camera body fully unwrapped, showing the Nikon logo, model badge, and serial number plate.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified/unknown condition, treated as worst case (possibly non-working or not a D750 at all)

risks.risk: Shutter count unknown; D750 bodies can have very high actuations despite cosmetic cleanliness.
risks.proof: A photo of the menu screen showing shutter count, or a shot from a shutter-count-checking app/service.

risks.risk: Sensor, mirror, or shutter mechanism fault (common D750 issue: shutter/aperture mechanism recall) not visible from boxed photos.
risks.proof: A test photo taken with the camera, plus a video of the shutter firing and live view working.

risks.risk: Mismatched or empty box scam pattern: sellers sometimes photograph only packaging, not the device, which is a known scam tactic.
risks.proof: An unboxing video or a photo of the camera powered on with date/time stamp or a handwritten note with today's date beside it.
risks.if_unproven: treated as high risk, not confirmed to contain a working D750

proof_requests: Clear photo of the actual camera body outside any packaging, showing Nikon logo, model name, and serial number.
Photo or video of the camera powered on, showing the rear LCD and menu screen with shutter count.
A test shot taken with the camera (ideally with today's date visible, e.g. on paper, in frame) to prove functionality.
Close-up of the lens mount and sensor for scratches, fungus, or dust.
Any proof of purchase or import documentation if 'American used' claim is to be relied on.
response.reason: All three photos show only retail packaging, manuals, and bubble-wrapped shapes; the camera body itself is never visible, so even a worst-case price cannot be fixed without confirming the actual item exists and matches the claimed model.
